text: Statistics released this week show retail sales rose 2.1% year on year, driven by clothing and household goods, though economists warned that consumer credit is rising faster than incomes.
The rand weakened against the dollar after the central bank kept interest rates unchanged, citing sticky food inflation.
A survey of small businesses in Gauteng found that 41% plan to hire in the next six months, the highest share since the survey began.
Fuel prices will rise by about 60 cents a litre next month, adding pressure on transport costs for commuters and freight operators.
The provincial health department says waiting times at three district hospitals fell after a new booking system for chronic medication was introduced.
Clinics in the Eastern Cape report a rise in measles cases among children who missed routine vaccinations, prompting a catch-up campaign.
A study of overdose admissions at an urban emergency unit found that most involved prescription painkillers combined with alcohol.
Nurses' unions warned that staff shortages in rural clinics are leading to longer queues and missed follow-up appointments.
Matric pass rates improved in four provinces, but participation in mathematics continued to decline.
A school feeding scheme pilot in KwaZulu-Natal was linked to higher attendance, according to an independent evaluation.
Universities warned that delays in student funding payments could force some first-year students to drop out.
Teachers in township schools say classrooms of more than 50 learners make individual attention almost impossible.
The power utility announced stage 2 load-shedding for the weekend after two generating units tripped.
A municipality signed agreements with independent producers to add 150 MW of solar capacity to its grid.
Hospitals in the province switched to diesel generators during last night's outages, raising concerns about fuel costs.
Households installing rooftop solar will need to register their systems with the municipality under new rules.
Police reported a drop in hijackings in the metro after increased patrols on major routes.
Residents blocked roads with burning tyres during a protest over service delivery, and police used rubber bullets to disperse the crowd.
A community policing forum launched a WhatsApp alert network for residents to report suspicious activity.
Copper cable theft caused signal failures that delayed commuter trains for several hours.
The auditor-general flagged irregular expenditure in several municipalities, citing poor record-keeping.
A parliamentary committee summoned the board of a state-owned company to explain delays in its annual report.
The electoral commission opened registration weekends ahead of local government elections.
Coalition partners in the metro council failed to agree on a budget, delaying payments to contractors.
Mining output fell for a third consecutive quarter as weak commodity demand weighed on exports.
A new TB testing van will visit farming communities in the Northern Cape every fortnight.
Early childhood development centres say subsidy payments are three months late, threatening staff salaries.
The national transmission company's new line will connect wind farms in the Eastern Cape to Gauteng.
Shopkeepers in the CBD hired private security after a spate of armed robberies.
The mayor survived a motion of no confidence after two smaller parties abstained.
Pharmacies report shortages of insulin pens as a supplier faces import delays.
Petrol stations in rural towns ran dry after a pipeline maintenance shutdown.
